firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and easily debuggable, following the core design principles and strategy mandates. It uses path-based ownership for user-specific data, ensuring clear authorization and efficient querying. The structure avoids hierarchical authorization dependencies by relying solely on `request.auth.uid` and path-based ownership, which simplifies security rules and allows atomic operations. Segregation of data based on access needs simplifies security rules by ensuring all documents in a collection share the same security requirements.

The `/users/{userId}` collection stores user profiles. The `/users/{userId}/landingPages/{landingPageId}` collection stores landing pages owned by each user. The `/users/{userId}/portalCustomizations/{portalCustomizationId}` collection stores portal customizations owned by each user. This structure facilitates straightforward security rules based on path-based ownership, guaranteeing that only the authenticated user can access their respective landing pages and portal customizations. All `list` operations are secured via path-based ownership, where listing a collection is only allowed if the authenticated user is the owner. 

This design emphasizes Authorization Independence, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), QAPs (Rules Are Not Filters), and structural segregation, resulting in a robust and maintainable data model.
